result:
Good — this is the only `*AgentTest.java` in the repo, and all other 30 tests pass.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/StrSubstitutorAgentTest.java` with 33 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering constructors, all `replace`/`replaceIn` overloads, escaping, default values, nested/cyclic variable resolution, custom lookups/prefixes/suffixes, and boundary cases.

33 tests run, 30 pass, 3 fail — and those 3 failures point to real bugs in `StrSubstitutor`, not test errors:

1. **`testConstructorRejectsNullPrefixWithIllegalArgumentException`** / **`testConstructorRejectsNullSuffixWithIllegalArgumentException`** — The javadoc for the `StrSubstitutor(Map, String, String)` constructor (and others) explicitly states `@throws IllegalArgumentException Thrown if the prefix or suffix is null.` However `setVariablePrefix(String)`/`setVariableSuffix(String)` use `Objects.requireNonNull(...)`, which throws `NullPointerException` instead. The documented contract and actual behavior disagree.

2. **`testStaticReplaceWithNullSourceAndNullPropertiesReturnsNull`** — The javadoc for `StrSubstitutor.replace(Object source, Properties valueProperties)` says `source ... null returns null`, but the implementation is:
   ```java
   if (valueProperties == null) {
       return source.toString();
   }
   ```
   When both `source` and `valueProperties` are `null`, this throws `NullPointerException` instead of returning `null`.
